ignoreInlineStyle exclusion

229 catalog sites use ignoreInlineStyle to opt regions out of inline theming. Upstream implements it as a per-element early return. Under declaration keying there is no early return available — one rule serves every element carrying that declaration, so an ignored element and a non-ignored element with the same style text share a rule. The exclusion has to move into the selector.

Every pair below carries the byte-identical style attribute. That is the whole point: if the exclusion is dropped, the two elements in a pair become indistinguishable to the emitter and both get themed.

.entry-content * — descendant combinator

IGNORED — must keep its own colours
THEMED — identical style attribute, must be themed

#panel > .row — child combinator

IGNORED
THEMED — identical attribute

a[href^="/store/apps/"] svg * — attribute selector in the chain

Escaped identifier — the catalog really contains these

IGNORED
THEMED — identical attribute
